title: Reduce complete nilpotent-Schur replay time by 9.15% (no κ)
body:
## Summary

The complete nilpotent-Schur replay from ssafwann's #5267 repeats exact immutable matrix products. A bounded 512-entry cache reduces its local median end-to-end wall time by **9.15%**, preserving every original fixture, check and scientific output byte.

```diff
 complete original replay
-  evaluate every matrix product again
+  reuse an identical ordered-matrix/modulus key, retaining at most 512 results
   run every original check and emit the unchanged scientific result
```

Claim type: scoped implementation-preservation proof, exact finite conformance and local performance evidence. The mathematical normal form, counts and original rejection controls remain the predecessor's results. This is an implementation contribution, not an independent audit of those results. No new kappa, supplier admission or selected-frontier change.

Nine new files in `research/schur-nilpotent-cache/` contain the wrapper, conformance checker, benchmark harness, generated raw measurements and source/task/replay metadata. Frozen sources retain their bytes and credit. This contribution was produced by Nick Petalas. Credit ssafwann / Malik Safwan, the retained Schur/header contributors and Python's standard bounded LRU implementation.

## Evidence

- Before: complete original entry point, median **2.271722 s**, range **2.193223–2.318187 s**.
- After: complete cached entry point, median **2.063804 s**, range **2.031170–2.248516 s**. All ten alternating fresh-process pairs improve; all twenty processes succeed with the identical scientific stdout hash. Generated `BENCHMARK.json` binds the original, implementation and harness bytes. The earlier five-pair pilot is retained separately because its overlapping ranges prompted the larger confirmation.
- Every one of **274,422** reached multiplication results agrees with the original computation. The cache reuses **128,609** calls and makes **145,813** misses, with a maximum reached matrix extent of 22. Eleven controls exercise source changes, capacity/eviction/retirement, factor order, modulus, immutable reuse and malformed operands.
- Complete scientific stdout remains SHA256 `ba358675b3031aef57895701547380f864223c83ef89a9f44f039714f1a97fa0`. The retained original workload and nine original rejection controls execute unchanged.
- Local CPython **3.12.15**, macOS arm64, standard library only. The host is shared; ranges overlap. This is repeated local wall-time evidence, not a guaranteed cross-machine speedup.
- Registered normal/optimized conformance and the actual cached entry point pass. Separately timed direct commands take **3.855 s**, **3.874 s** and **2.101 s**, respectively, rounded upward. Metadata/pins, warning-strict in-memory compilation, function-size inspection, whitespace checks and committed-byte/source-history preflight pass at `5b6ca76a176bbc81500d44b89a499d8cdd85809a`.

From the worktree root, using the exact local interpreter path:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -B research/schur-nilpotent-cache/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -O -W error -B research/schur-nilpotent-cache/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -B research/schur-nilpotent-cache/cached.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/schur-nilpotent-cache
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/schur-nilpotent-cache --check-source-history
```

Expected markers are `PASS_SCHUR_NILPOTENT_CACHE calls=274422 hits=128609 controls=11`, `PASS_SCHUR_NILPOTENT_EXTENSION`, `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE` and `PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES`. Substitute any CPython 3.12 interpreter outside this environment.

To repeat the complete performance experiment, choose a new output path outside the checkout:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -B research/schur-nilpotent-cache/benchmark.py --rounds 10 --output /absolute/external/new-measurement.json
```

## Limitations and unrun obligations

The proof covers this pinned replay's immutable tuple inputs. Mutable inputs, other source revisions, other cache capacities and different consumers need their own contract. The source digest rejects changed executable bytes before execution; cache lifetime ends after one invocation. Python's managed allocation, authenticated executable loading and this one replaced call target are bounded deviations documented in the README.

All registered commands passed locally and in hosted CI. Hosted replay certifies exact conformance, source/measurement bindings and the complete cached entry point. It does not repeat local timings or certify a speedup on another machine. No selected cold replay, native supplier/caller/precision/stock/outer proof, Lean, Docker, independent human review or proof-kernel acceptance is claimed.

## Open next questions

Can this bounded reuse boundary help one separately named active replay? Start with its actual profile, immutable repeated-product contract and complete end-to-end workload. No other source or consumer is covered here; optimization stops at this first verified improvement.

## Related open work

No open PR in the refreshed source/object search studies the PR5267 complete replay or its product runtime. The merged #5287, #5343, #5348 and #5360 develop mathematical Schur follow-ups; those results are cited context and are not reverified or extended here. Unpublished work and arbitrary diffs remain outside overlap coverage.

Before DONE, the completion refresh inspected all twelve other open PRs created by this account since the advance claim. They concern other replay fixtures, dyadic capacities, matcher routes, tensor reconstruction, recursion costs, ternary COPY, Gaussian bounds, rank-exchange credit and faithful label widths. None studies this exact complete replay or reports a competing timing for it. No additional computations were run to check those contributions.

[Advance claim](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19362895). Canonical main was refreshed before commit at `7c49fe32c55de02c2c873655c804b16e4c3fef0a`; relevant guidance and inputs were unchanged.

## CI notes

Both hosted checks passed at exact head `5b6ca76a176bbc81500d44b89a499d8cdd85809a` in [run 41550378276](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/41550378276): [plan](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/41550378276/job/125636203093) in 4m37s and [replay (research/schur-nilpotent-cache)](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/actions/runs/41550378276/job/125638146628) in 1m36s. The completed checks were read once. Separate run metadata confirms the matching head, completed status and success.

Hosted execution passed all three registered commands: normal/optimized complete conformance and the actual cached entry point. The direct verifier, metadata/pins and publication byte/history checks also pass locally. The timing experiment remains local performance evidence; independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

## Merge danger

Door: two-way. Blast radius: isolated package. No shared code, frozen predecessor, selected record or frontier is changed.
